questions.question: The present age of Ramesh is 7 years more than the present age of his wife Sangeeta. 6 years hence, the age of Ramesh will be three times that of his son Mayank. If the present age of Mayank is 10 years, then what is the present age of Sangeeta?
questions.solution:
Let the present age of Ramesh be 'R', Sangeeta be 'S', and that of Mayank be 'M'.

(1) The present age of Ramesh is 7 years more than the present age of his wife Sangeeta. 

.

(2) 6 years hence, the age of Ramesh will be three times that of his son Mayank. If the present age of Mayank is 10 years, **implies M = 10,**

⇒ (R + 6) = 3 × (M + 6)

⇒ (R + 6) = 3 × (10 + 6)

⇒ R + 6 = 3 × 16

⇒ R + 6 = 48 

⇒ R = 48 - 6

⇒ R = 42

Then, we know R = 7 + S,

⇒ S + 7 = 42

⇒ S = 42 - 7

⇒ S = 35 years

Hence, **35 years **is the correct answer.

There are three books coded as A, B and C. The price of book A is twice the price of book B and one-third the price of book C. If book C costs Rs. 84, then what are the costs of book A and book B, respectively?
questions.solution:
Given:

Three books coded as A, B and C.

1) The price of book A is twice the price of book B

=> A = 2B → eq. 1

2) The price of book A is one-third the price of book C

=> A = 1/3 C → eq. 2

3) Book C costs Rs. 84

Put the value in eq. 2

=> A = 1/3 × 84

**=> A = 28**

Put the value of A in eq 1;

=> A = 2B

=> 28 = 2B

=> B = 28 ÷ 2

**=> B = 14**

Hence, the costs of book A and book B, respectively **“****Rs. 28 and Rs. 14”.**

In a class, if 3 students are absent, then the rest of the students can be divided equally into 7 groups and if 7 students are absent, then the rest of the students can be divided equally into 9 groups. How many students are present in the class?
questions.solution:
Let, the total number of students are x.

If 3 students are absent, then the rest of the students can be divided equally into 7 groups.

Equal parts are (x - 3)/7

If 7 students are absent, then the rest of the students can be divided equally into 9 groups. 

Equal parts are (x - 7)/9

According to the question,

(x - 3)/7 = (x - 7)/9 + 4

⇒ (9x - 27 - 7x + 49)/ 63 = 4

⇒ 2x + 22 = 63 × 4

⇒ 2x = 252 - 22

⇒ 2x = 230

⇒ x = 115.

Hence, the correct answer is **"115"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** By option elimination:

**__Option (1):__ 115**

If 3 students are absent, then the rest of the students can be divided equally into 7 groups. 

Equal parts are (115 - 3)/7 =112 / 7 = 16

If 7 students are absent, then the rest of the students can be divided equally into 9 groups. 

Equal parts are (115 - 7)/9 = 108 / 9 = 12 

**Therefore two conditions are satisfied. **

__Option (2):__ 140

If 3 students are absent, then the rest of the students can be divided equally into 7 groups. 

Equal parts are (140 - 3)/7 =**137 does not divide by 7.**

__Option (3____):__ 87

If 3 students are absent, then the rest of the students can be divided equally into 7 groups. 

Equal parts are (87 - 3)/7 = 84/7 = 12.

If 7 students are absent, then the rest of the students can be divided equally into 9 groups. 

Equal parts are (87 - 7)/9 = **80 does not divide by 9.**

__Option (4____): __101

If 3 students are absent, then the rest of the students can be divided equally into 7 groups. 

Equal parts are (101 - 3)/7 = 98/7 = 14.

If 7 students are absent, then the rest of the students can be divided equally into 9 groups. 

Equal parts are (101 - 7)/9 = **94 does not divide by 9.**

Hence, the correct answer is "115".

questions.question: In an entrance test, Tiwari scored 25% marks and failed by 64 marks. If he had scored 40% marks, then he would have secured 32 marks more than the pass marks. Find the pass marks.
questions.solution:
**Let,**

**X is the passing mark**

**Y is the total marks.**

**Given:**

**1) **Tiwari scored 25% marks and failed by 64 marks.

X – 64 = 25%Y **-------- eq. (1)**

2) He had scored 40% marks, then he would have secured 32 marks more than the pass marks.

X + 32 = 40%Y **-------- eq. (2)**

**Subtract eq. (2) from eq. (1)**

=> (X + 32) – (X – 64) = 40%Y - 25%Y

=> 32 + 64 = 15%Y

=> 96 = 15%Y

=> Y = 96 ÷ (15/100)</p&
